title: Erskine Tate, Plantation, Dave Peyton and Dipper Mouth Blues
summary: Louis moved to the Vendome while Joe played with Erskine Tate and at small spots, then the Plantation with Dave Peyton. Joe sold Dipper Mouth Blues outright before going to New York.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, they worked a long time together and things began to get bad again. Then Louie went over to the, what's the name of this, theater on, uh, State Street. State near 35th. Oh, the Vandome was that? Uh-huh. And then Dome. Louie went then over to play there. They sort of split. Joe didn't have much work and we went over there and he played. He played for a long time with, uh, I think it must have been, with, uh, Tate. Oh, yes. Yes, I knew him. Erskine Tate. Erskine Tate, right. And they played and it was quite a success for a long time. Then all the time Joe was playing this, little hole in the wall, I call them, like the Pecan and Miss Major. And of course it kept him quite busy. Then he got this big job, plantation. That was a big job. It was black and tan. It was on, on South Park and 35th. And with Peyton. Peyton had a review there. Dave Peyton. I met him once in Chicago. Joe played with him, but he didn't care so much for, Joe didn't care so much for him. So from there, after that was closed down, that's the time Joe went to New York. But he made quite a success around Chicago. Yes, I knew him. Playing at the Dreamland with all the actors and playing at the Peking. And he made quite a success. He made a name for himself. That's where he began to go over. Began to be in here. And he made Dipper Mouth Blues. Yes. That's Joe's own number. That's our own number. He composed that. But he told me that was the first piece he ever made. And he sold it outright. He sold it. How about that? That's too bad. Just for a few pennies. He said he didn't know any different. Well, I don't know. It went from that bad to worse after he went to New York. Because nobody sent for him in New York. He just went there on a wild goose chase just for two or three nights for a week staying. Well, it wasn't a success. His band wasn't a success. Or was with him then. And Blue Trey. And Red Alum. Red Alum. And Nicholson. Nickson. Albin Nicholos. Yes.
